Ono
OH-no
proper noun
Hebrew ’ono, “vigorous” or “strong,” a town built by the Benjamites, in the plain of Ono, resettled after the captivity.

Biblical Definition

Ono was a town builded by the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin, who builded Ono and Lod, with the towns thereof (1Ch 8:12). Its men returned from the captivity of Babylon with Zerubbabel, the children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono being numbered among the remnant that came again to the land (Ezr 2:33), and it is named with Lod among the dwelling-places of Benjamin in the valley of craftsmen after the return (Neh 11:35). In the days of Nehemiah, when the wall of Jerusalem was building, the adversaries Sanballat and Geshem sent unto him, saying, Come, let us meet together in some one of the villages in the plain of Ono; but they thought to do him mischief, and Nehemiah answered, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down (Neh 6:2). Thus the plain of Ono became the scene of a faithful servant’s steadfastness, who would not leave the LORD’s work to parley with His enemies. The dictionary honours that the LORD kept this Benjamite town through building, exile, and return, and made its plain a witness to holy resolution. Ono stands as a token that the providence of God preserves the places and the people of His promise, and that the servant set to a great work must not come down from it at the bidding of them that seek his hurt.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town built by the Benjamites, in the plain of Ono, resettled after the captivity.

expand to see more

ONO, a town built by the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin.

The name signifies “vigorous” or “strong.”

Its men returned from the Babylonian captivity with Zerubbabel.

It lay in a plain, named the plain of Ono, in the valley of craftsmen.

It witnesses to Nehemiah’s steadfast refusal to leave the LORD’s work.

Key Scripture

1Ch 8:12 — "The sons of Elpaal; Eber, and Misham, and Shamed, who built Ono, and Lod, with the towns thereof:"

Ezr 2:33 — "The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty and five."

Neh 6:2 — "That Sanballat and Geshem sent unto me, saying, Come, let us meet together in some one of the villages in the plain of Ono. But they thought to do me mischief."

Neh 11:35 — "Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen."

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to holy steadfastness in the work of the LORD.

expand to see more

Ono is a town of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name in the building of Benjamin, in the return of the captivity, and in the days of Nehemiah may know it for a real town kept by a real God through the generations.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is steadfastness in the work of the LORD against every distraction. He who set the Benjamites to build Ono is the same who upheld Nehemiah when the enemy called him down to the plain of Ono, that he might not leave the wall to parley. The saint pressed to forsake his appointed labour may remember Nehemiah’s word, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down, and hold his post for the LORD.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “vigorous,” Ono names a Benjamite town in the plain of Ono.

Ono — Hebrew ’ono, “vigorous” or “strong.”

It was built by the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin.

Its men returned from the Babylonian captivity with Zerubbabel.

It lay in the plain of Ono, in the valley of craftsmen.

Its plain was where Nehemiah’s adversaries sought to call him down.

Usage

"Like Nehemiah in the plain of Ono, the servant of God must not leave a great work to parley with His enemies."

"The LORD who kept Ono through building, exile, and return preserves the places of His promise."

"I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down, is the word of every faithful labourer."
